questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against designing for an imagined, averaged-out 'the business' instead of mapping real stakeholders?
options: Because Salesforce requires a named stakeholder list before any project can begin
Because each business unit and region has its own leadership and priorities, and ignoring that produces a design that satisfies no one particularly well
Because stakeholders are legally required to approve every Salesforce configuration change
Because there is only ever one true business priority at any company
questions.explain: LTV Global's four business units and three regions each have distinct priorities; designing for a single averaged 'the business' voice produces a design that doesn't actually fit any of the real stakeholders well.

questions.q: Which stakeholder is described as the most sensitive to performance and scale, given their business unit's transaction volume?
options: The CFO / Head of Finance
The Director of Field Service (EMEA)
The VP of Parts & Aftermarket Distribution (Global)
The Chief Information Security & Compliance Officer
questions.explain: The VP of Parts & Aftermarket Distribution owns the highest-volume business unit and is called out as the most sensitive to performance, since any slowdown versus today's tools is a non-starter for this stakeholder.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as one of the four business drivers actually pushing LTV Global to fund this transformation now?
options: A legal mandate requiring every multinational to use Salesforce
Fragmentation across business units seeing incomplete, disconnected pictures of the same customers
A requirement from Salesforce that all customers migrate off legacy CRMs within five years
A one-time tax incentive for enterprise software modernization
questions.explain: Fragmentation (along with growth, cost, and competitive pressure) is one of the four real business drivers this lesson names as justifying the transformation.

questions.q: Which stakeholder does this lesson identify as owning ultimate accountability for the project's success to leadership, and who presents the design to the Architecture Review Board?
options: The CIO, as executive sponsor
Dealers and end customers
The Director of Field Service (EMEA)
The VP of Equipment Sales (North America)
questions.explain: The lesson names the CIO as the executive sponsor who owns the overall technology budget and identity provider relationship, and who ultimately presents the design, through the architect, to the ARB.

questions.q: The lesson points to a tension between the Parts & Aftermarket VP's performance demands and which other stakeholder's priority?
options: The dealers' and end customers' desire for self-service ordering
The CFO's caution about touching the legacy financial system
The Director of Field Service's zero-disruption cutover demand
The CIO's ownership of the identity provider relationship
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly names the tension between the Parts & Aftermarket VP's performance demands and the CFO's caution about the financial system as one of the real stakeholder tensions this capstone has to resolve later (in the integration lessons).
